answer: For standard reimbursement claims, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2]. For Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is extended to 60 days from discharge [5]. An archived 2024 policy previously listed the deadline as 15 days from the date of discharge [3].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on retail plans and Top-Up/Super Top-Up plans, unless explicitly waived in writing by Aurora [3][5][7]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan (for ages 60 and above), the waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].

As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1]. However, because hospitals join and leave the network continuously, this number is indicative, and the authoritative list is found in the Aurora app and portal hospital locator [1].

Under the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. Making a claim does not reduce the accumulated bonus; it only stops accumulating for that specific year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment because IVF, infertility, and assisted reproduction are listed as permanent exclusions [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the dispute to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response remains unsatisfactory or if they do not respond within 30 days of your original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

All plans include road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1][6]. In addition, the Aurora Gold plan provides air ambulance coverage of up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. It is subject to the standard 30-day initial waiting period, with no separate waiting period applied [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. A new policyholder may cancel within 15 days of receiving the policy document, or 30 days for policies sold through distance marketing, and receive a refund of the premium minus the proportionate risk premium for the cover period, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [1][2].
You earn 150 wellness points per year for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora does not use a TPA and administers its own claims directly [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid because proportionate deduction will apply [1][8]. With a ₹5,00,000 sum insured on the Silver plan, your room-rent limit is 2% or ₹10,000 per day, giving an eligibility ratio of 0.667 for a ₹15,000 per day room [1][2]. Consequently, all charges tied to the room category (such as room rent, surgeon fees, and nursing/OT) will be proportionately reduced, while items like pharmacy and consumables remain fully payable [5][8].
